posts.name: Roger the Alien
posts.cooked:
Do you prefer to play with or without open hand if playing online?

I think it‘s more interesting to play without open hand as you won‘t know what will happen. 

This also encourages to communicate „Wait, I will play heroic interception next turn, if you have oblivion in your hand play it next turn“.

I also think it‘s interesting to let other players make their own decisions and sometimes others could just always suggest what to do. 

In my opinion open hand is only worth to explain this game others and teach them some strategies or whatever but otherwise I am not interested. 

What‘s about you?

posts.name: dmiitrie
posts.cooked:
I don’t really see much of a point playing with closed hands.  In my experience, people end up just telling everyone else what they have practically all the time. And in cases where that doesn’t completely happen, people often wish it had.  Stuff like, “wait, how long have you had that Heroic Interception?  Now I wish I hadn’t discarded my Oblivion last turn!”

And as far as alpha players go, that’s kind of just a risk you’re always going to take with coop games, especially when you play with strangers.  I don’t believe closed hands inhibit them any more than open hands do.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked: I've never seen any reason to hide your hand in a game like this. Especially this one. Imagine playing as the Adept, for example - "Okay, I can let someone play a card now...umm, so what does everyone actually have?", and then having to wait while everyone tells you and then try to figure out the best play from that. As opposed to just looking at what everyone's got out and going "Okay, how about if X plays <card> because then that will deal with Y...". I would find it so frustrating if no-one would want to show what cards they have when I kind of need to see them :P.

posts.name: grysqrl
posts.cooked:
I strongly dislike playing with open hands. I find that just being able to click on what you want someone to play vastly lowers the barrier to alpha-ing. It feels frustrating - I don't like people telling me what to do. I'd rather play more slowly and have a discussion if other players care what I'm doing. Alternately, I'm totally fine shooting from the hip and playing non-optimally most of the time.

Either way, I'll usually ignore/avoid suggestions made by people who just click on the options they think I should take without saying anything about it.

posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked:
I've never played anything but the IOS version, and that solo.

That said, if you're not teaching the game, it seems like the correct way is to play with closed hands, and invert the discussion. Rather than "you should play this card," I'd say players should limit themselves to "I'm thinking of playing this card. Does that work well for you, or do you have a reason I should save it for a later turn?" I.e. never tell anyone else what to play, and don't ask what they have, but if you think coordination is important, ask for it in regard to what you're playing, not what they're playing.

I'm not sure you can get quarterbacking types to agree to that, though.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Oh I don't tell people what to play. If someone is puzzling over their options I'll instead point at whatever the villain/environment decks currently have out and say stuff like "Well, this thing is a pretty major threat right now - is there anything you can do to help with that?". Also, if I'm teaching and someone asks me about a specific card, it kind of helps if I can see it, in case I need to double-check the wording or something (many of the older decks I've got memorised pretty well by now, but by no means every deck in the game ;)). Also, if people can see my hand, it better helps me explain whatever I'm planning for my next turn, or whatever, should I need to go into any more detail than "I'm gonna deal with X on my turn so don't worry about it", or "Don't worry about not being able to do that thing along with the other thing because I can let you do that when we get to my turn", etc.

I dunno, it just feels...wrong (if that's the right word) for people to be keeping their resources from each other when the whole point of the game is that we're working together and need to know what each other is capable of.

posts.name: Phantom5613
posts.cooked:
I prefer closed when it comes to digital.

It's for the same reasons that have been coming up: Avoids alpha/annoying players from trying to lead me by the nose, lets me and others think for themselves unless they ask for help, let's me focus on my hand and what I can do, and encourages communication between players opposed to just clicking on a card and expecting someone's intent to be clear.

I never find the digital game to go so fast that there isn't a moment for a quick question or such, such as asking someone "Can you do this?" or "I can give a draw or play: Who wants what?" I usually don't have access to voice, but typing something out usually only take s a few moments anyway.
